messages:
sara_sales: FYI VennHealth doing a geo-failover POC and they hit a bunch of 429s when we moved traffic to eu-west-1. They say it looks bursty — short spikes of errors during a replayed session.

alex_eng: Can you paste one of the request ids and a short snippet of the client log? Also which model + route are they hitting?

sara_sales: Request sample: `req_20260218_34ab` — route `/v1/generate` model `redwood-open-13b`. Client log shows `HTTP 429` immediate after a sequence of large prompts. They were ramping token usage for a tenant-wide test.

olivia_se: Do we know if this is per-tenant token budget or per-route cap? Sometimes large prompts exhaust token budget even if rps looks fine.

mike_infra: Pulling logs now. I see the gateway returning these headers for that req id: 
```
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 167
X-Token-Budget-Remaining: 4800
```
Looks like per-route remaining hit 0 at the spike moment.

alex_eng: That Reset looks short (167s). Could be their burst window + refill rate not matching the replayed pattern. Also large prompts use more tokens so token-budget might be depleted shortly after.

sara_sales: Customer says they replayed user sessions (multi-turn) which include a 6k token system prompt. That probably blew the token budget. They expected per-request throttles instead of per-route.

mike_infra: Two quick checks: 1) confirm their tenant plan (limits differ for trial vs paid), 2) check if we applied any custom per-route caps for that account during onboarding. I'm seeing a custom cap set last week: per-route cap = 100 r/min for `/v1/generate` for tenant `vennhealth`.

olivia_se: @sara_sales can you confirm plan? If they're on trial we normally have lower burst allowances. If they need higher for POC we can temp bump.

sara_sales: They are on a POC reserved trial (sales-managed). Requested higher burst for 48h to finish replay.

alex_eng: If we want a quick mitigation: increase per-route cap and token-burst window for that tenant, or enable temporary override to route those requests to dedicated pool. Which is faster?

mike_infra: Quickest is a per-tenant per-route override. I can add +200 r/min and raise token refill rate for 24h. Will need approval from CS.

sara_sales: Approved by CS on call. Please do the override.

deploy-bot: action_log: created override for tenant=vennhealth route=/v1/generate delta_rate=200 delta_token_refill=+4000 duration=24h by=mike_infra

mike_infra: Done. I also adjusted the burst window from 60s -> 120s for that override so queued bursts smooth out.

olivia_se: After change, can the customer run the replay again and capture any 429s + the gateway headers?

sara_sales: They're starting the run now. I'll paste results in ~10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex_eng: If they still see 429s, collect the full request payload size (tokens used) and the exact timestamps; we'll correlate with refill ticks. Also include `x-request-id` and `x-route-shard` headers.

sara_sales: Run complete — they report 2x 429s in first 90s, then clean. Here are gateway headers from one error:
```
x-request-id: req_20260218_34ab
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1400
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 95
X-Token-Budget-Remaining: 1200
x-route-shard: eu-west-1-a
```

mike_infra: That pattern (early 429s then clear) is exactly burst-exhaustion then refill. We can further smooth by increasing initial token bucket size for the tenant or pre-warming caches. For POC it's fine to keep override til end of test.

olivia_se: Noted — we'll draft a short doc for sales on how to explain burst vs sustained limits to customers and the temporary override process. Can someone capture the commands we used to apply the override?

mike_infra: Command I ran: 
```
# internal infra cli
infractl tenant override create --tenant vennhealth --route /v1/generate --rate +200 --token-refill +4000 --window 120s --duration 24h
```

sara_sales: Great, I'll send the customer the summary and confirm no more 429s in their end-to-end tests. Thanks team :tada:

alex_eng: Follow-up item: product should consider a POC preset profile that temporarily increases burst allowances for replay-style tests (with audit logs) so sales doesn't need manual ops for every POC.

olivia_se: Filed a follow-up ticket in product backlog.

sara_sales: Closing thread once I get final confirmation from VennHealth.
